blocks.x: How Data & Lakehouse lands in Capabilities — the constraints that shape the build, the gated delivery pattern, and the deltas we commit against your baseline.

In Insurance & Risk, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Claims, policy and exposure data fragmented
Underwriting, claims and finance each hold their own truth; loss triangles reconcile by spreadsheet. Portfolio analytics that should steer the cycle take months of manual assembly.
Claims intake drowning in documents

FNOL packets, medical reports, repair estimates and police files arrive as unstructured documents; manual triage queues claims for days before an adjuster sees them. Leakage and customer patience both bleed in the queue.
Pricing sophistication outrunning governance

GLM-based pricing, telematics factors and external data enrichment multiply model complexity faster than validation capacity. Filings get challenged; model risk documentation is reconstructed under exam pressure.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: IFRS 17 / LDTI accounting and DORA (for EU insurers). ICT third-party and resilience obligations like banking peers. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The rhythm is fixed on purpose: progress becomes visible from week one, not after the first steering meeting. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
